newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV RULES HIMSELF OUT, FAVOURS MUSTER.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-KAFELNIKOV RULES HIMSELF OUT, FAVOURS MUSTER.

text.p: French Open champion Yevgeny Kafelnikov said on Sunday he was unlikely to win the crown again this year and Thomas Muster should be regarded as the favourite.
"It would take a miracle for me to retain my title", Kafelnikov, who became the first Russian to triumph on the Paris clay a year ago, told a news conference.
The 23-year-old from the Black Sea resort of Sotchi, who opens his defence against Czech Martin Damm on Monday, was sidelined for three months this season with a broken finger in his right hand.
He struggled in his first outings after his recovery but showed some progress recently by reaching the quarter-finals in Rome and the semifinals in Hamburg.
"I feel a hundred percent fit now but I still need time to recapture my best tennis," said Kafelnikov, looking forward to his first match.
"It will be a very important test for me. What I need now is to win matches to restore my confidence. Hopefully, I'll just play better and better."
Asked who he thought had the best chance of succeeding him, Kafelnikov named Austrian Muster, the 1995 winner.

"I know he hasn't been playing very well in his last tournaments on clay but I can't see anybody beating him, apart maybe from (Spain's) Albert Costa," he said. "When Thomas is playing best of five sets on clay, he's really tough to beat."
Kafelnikov laughed when somebody asked him who he would like to meet in the final. "If I reach the final, I will be very, very happy," he said.
The gifted young Russian might not be too ambitious for this year's French Open but he does hope to be back to his brilliant best in the near future.

"My win last year made me realise that I was a good overall player," he said. "I never thought I could win the French Open because clay was not my favourite surface. I thought I had much more chances of winning the U.S. Open or the Australian Open.

"Now I know I can win anywhere. I'm only 23 and I feel there are still plenty of good things ahead of me. Obviously I would like to become the number one sometime but it wouldn't be realistic for me to think that it could happen tomorrow. I'll just have to be patient."
